title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook: Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, Status Page & Comms Templates
author: Michael Chen
body:
Summary

This document codifies Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response (IR) processes: severity classification, alerting & escalation, playbook/runbook actions for common failure modes, postmortem expectations, rotation and backup policies, game-day exercises, and canonical status page and customer communications templates. It is the single source of truth for responders and incident reviewers and is intended for SRE, serving runtime, infra, platform, and product engineering teams.

Goals and scope

- Restore customer-facing functionality quickly and safely.
- Minimize customer impact and communication gaps.
- Capture actionable root causes and long-term remediation in postmortems.
- Maintain a predictable, well-tested on-call culture (rotations, backups, game days).

Entities & services referenced

Primary service names used in runbooks and examples below: inference-gateway, model-router, kv-cache, batch-scheduler, real-time-proxy, metrics-pipeline, control-plane-api, console-api, auth-service. Alerts and escalation are configured in PagerDuty (service names), Slack (#incidents, #sre-oncall), and Datadog (dashboards and monitors).

SLAs & SLOs (operational thresholds)

- Hosted text-generation API availability SLO: 99.95% (rolling 30d). Error budget policy: if 30d rolling availability drops below 99.90%, escalate to Exec + Platform.
- Latency SLO (inference-gateway): P95 < 150ms for short prompts (<256 tokens), P99 < 500ms.
- Embeddings API SLO: 99.9% availability; P95 < 120ms.
- Alert thresholds (examples):
  - 5xx rate > 2% (5m) on inference-gateway -> SEV1
  - Increase in P99 response time > 2x baseline (15m rolling) -> SEV1
  - Total token throughput drop > 30% platform-wide (10m) -> SEV1
  - Sidecar/worker OOMs > 1% (10m) -> SEV2
  - Partial degradation (single-region errors) -> SEV2

Severity classification & routing

1) SEV0 (Extinction): Multi-region outage affecting >50% production traffic, or major data loss. Immediate Exec page + all-hands.
2) SEV1 (Major outage): Significant customer impact (failed requests or latency causing SLA breaches). Full IR runbook. PagerDuty high-priority page to on-call SRE + product lead.
3) SEV2 (Partial degradation): Reduced functionality for subset of customers / single region. On-call handles with followups and fixes.
4) SEV3 (Minor/Engineering task): Degraded non-critical metrics or delayed jobs; ticket created, no all-hands.

Incident roles & responsibilities

- Incident Commander (IC): Directs remediation, prioritizes tasks, and owns timeline. Usually the SRE on-call or senior engineer from owning team.
- Communications Lead (Comms): Updates status page, Slack incident channel, and external comms.
- Subject Matter Experts (SME): Engineers from owning services (e.g., model-router, kv-cache).
- Triage Lead: First responder who validates alerts and assigns severity.
- Postmortem Author: Usually IC or owning-team engineer; coordinates write-up within 72 hours.

Escalation & communication channels

- Primary paging: PagerDuty. Escalation policy: on-call -> backup on-call after 15 minutes -> team lead after 30 minutes -> SRE manager after 60 minutes.
- Slack incident channels: create private channel named incident-YYYYMMDD-<short-sev>-<service>. Examples: incident-20260304-sev1-inference-gateway.
- Email & external comms: Communications Lead uses templates in this doc.
- Status page: status.redwood.ai (internal write API: control-plane-api/status).

Runbooks (common incidents)

A. SEV1: inference-gateway 5xx spike

1) Triage (first 10 minutes)
   - Confirm the alert in Datadog: monitor data -> inference-gateway > 5xx rate.
   - Check PagerDuty payload and logs: PagerDuty -> alert -> event details.
   - Open Slack incident channel, ping on-call and IC.

2) Immediate mitigations (10-30 minutes)
   - If recent deploy detected: rollback via CI pipeline (ci-cd -> rollback job) or promote prior tag. Document deployment ID and timeline.
   - If autoscaling thrash suspected: inspect batch-scheduler and node metrics; temporarily scale up pool (kubectl scale deploy/gateway --replicas=N) or increase instance size via infra runbook.
   - If error indicates model-router mapping failure: switch traffic to fallback model using model-router admin API: POST /admin/route?action=promote&model=fallback-v1 (auth via kubectl port-forward to control-plane-api).

3) Restore & verify (30-60 minutes)
   - Validate reduced 5xx rate and P99 latency on inference-gateway dashboard.
   - If rollback used, keep monitoring for 60 minutes before reattempting the deploy in a canary fashion.

4) Post-incident
   - IC assigns postmortem author and sets severity.
   - Comms updates status page and customer emails (templates below).

B. SEV1: model load failures on model-router

- Symptoms: repeated model load errors in model-router logs (OOM, corrupted weights), SDK call returns 503 with message "model unavailable".
- Immediate actions:
  1) Identify affected model versions: kubectl logs model-router | grep "failed to load".
  2) If crashloopbackoff across replicas, gather crashlogs and core dumps to /tmp/incident-<id>/diagnostics.
  3) Promote earlier healthy model via model-router admin endpoint and route traffic away from failing servers.
  4) If due to quantization profile mismatch, revert to FP32/quantization_profile=stable-2025 via control-plane-api.

- Longer term: add pre-deploy model validation gate in model-onboarding (automated load smoke tests on staging GPUs).

C. SEV2: degraded kv-cache hit rate causing latency increase

- Symptoms: cache hit rate < 60% (baseline 85%) and backend latency spikes.
- Steps:
  1) Check metrics-pipeline and cache nodes (redis-cluster) health.
  2) If node unavailable, failover using redis-sentinel playbook: redis-cli -h sentinel-host SENTINEL FAILOVER mymaster.
  3) Clear rollbacks: if stale entries cause inefficiency, consider TTL tuning vs eviction policy change (cfg: maxmemory-policy volatile-lru). Test in canary.

Runbook template (how-to use)

- Always record timestamps (UTC) and all commands run. Place artifacts in /incidents/<incident-id>/ (S3 bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/incident-<id>).
- If rolling back a deploy, include commit hash, CI job ID, and the operator who initiated it.
- All network/infra escalations must be coordinated with CloudOps via slack @cloudops.

Postmortem process & template

Timeline:
- Initial postmortem draft due within 72 hours.
- Final postmortem published within 7 days with assigned remediation owners and target dates.

Postmortem template (plain text)
- Title: consistent prefix: PM-[YYYYMMDD]-<service>-<sev>
- Summary: one-paragraph impact summary
- Severity & scope: sev, affected regions/customers, duration
- Detection: who/what (monitor, customer, PagerDuty) and detection time
- Timeline: ordered timestamps (UTC) of events and actions (bulleted)
- Root cause analysis: short description + evidence (logs, traces, config diffs)
- Immediate mitigations: what was done to restore service
- Long-term remediation & action items: owner, description, ETA (YYYY-MM-DD)
- Follow-ups: monitoring improvements, runbook updates, capacity changes, onboarding tests
- Lessons learned & risk assessment
- Links: logs, dashboards, incident artifacts, PRs, and rollback IDs

Postmortem ownership: IC assigns a postmortem author within 4 hours of severity classification. The owning team completes the analysis and tracks action items in the engineering backlog (Jira project: ENG-IR).

On-call rotations & backups

- Rotation cadence: weekly rotations by default (Mon 09:00 UTC -> next Mon 09:00 UTC).
- Primary on-call responsibilities: first responder, incident triage, runbook execution, postmortem initiation.
- Backup on-call: scheduled person who covers escalations if primary does not acknowledge within 15 minutes.
- Coverage rules:
  - Holidays: primary calls must have documented coverage; SRE manager will ensure backup coverage.
  - Shift swaps: must be logged in the on-call calendar and a handoff checklist posted in Slack.

Game days (exercises)

Purpose: validate runbooks, test multi-team coordination, and validate monitoring/alerts.

- Frequency: quarterly platform-wide game day + monthly team-level tabletop or automated simulation.
- Typical scenarios:
  - Full-region loss simulation (failover control-plane API and route traffic to backup region)
  - High-P99 latency from model-router causing cascading queueing
  - Redis cluster partial outage and KV-cache degradation
  - Model onboarding bad artifact deployed (automated rollback test)

Game day plan checklist:
1) Objectives and scope (pre-approved)
2) Participants and roles (IC, ops, comms, SMEs)
3) Run the scenario with a controlled blast-radius
4) Record metrics and timelines and collect qualitative feedback
5) Post-game retrospective and action items logged (Jira ENG-IR)

Status page & customer comms templates

Status page guidelines:
- Use concise, non-technical headlines for external viewers. Include impact, affected services, regions, and ETA if known.
- Update frequency: every 30 minutes until resolved, then once at incident close with summary.
- Internal status details (more technical) go to incident Slack channel.

External status page templates:

1) Degraded performance (short)
- Title: Partial degradation: Text generation latency increased
- Body: We are investigating increased latency for text generation requests affecting a subset of customers in us-west-2. Some requests may take longer than expected or time out. Our on-call team is actively investigating. We will update in 30 minutes.

2) Service outage (short)
- Title: Service outage: Text generation API returning errors
- Body: We are experiencing errors for the text generation API affecting most customers in multiple regions. Engineers are working to restore service. We will update in 15 minutes.

Customer email template (post-incident)

Subject: Incident report — [Date] — [Service] — [Brief impact]

Hi [Customer name],

We want to follow up on the incident on [YYYY-MM-DD] that affected [service]. Summary: [one-paragraph impact and duration].

Root cause: [brief root cause].
Actions taken: [short bullets of mitigations and timeline].
Next steps & prevention: [remediation & ETA].

We apologize for the disruption. If you have additional questions, please reply to this email and your account team will follow up.

Best,
Redwood Inference Operations Team

Operational tooling & runbook hygiene

- Incident artifacts must be stored in s3://redwood-incidents/incident-<id> with folder structure: diagnostics/, logs/, traces/, screenshots/, postmortem.md.
- Runbook ownership: each service must declare runbook owner in initial service on-call onboarding doc (owner_team + primary contact). Runbooks are reviewed quarterly and after any SEV1/SEV0 incident.
- Metrics & dashboards: maintain a minimal incident dashboard per service with: availability, total requests, 5xx rate, P95/P99 latency, error budget burn, and downstream queue length.

Compliance & exec reporting

- SEV0/SEV1 incidents trigger an executive summary: sent to CTO, Head of Product, Head of Customer Success within 24 hours.
- For customer-impacting incidents > 4 hours, Legal and Finance are notified for potential SLA credits.

Appendices

- Useful commands (examples):
  - Inspect gateway pods: kubectl -n platform get pods -l app=inference-gateway -o wide
  - Tail logs: kubectl -n platform logs -f deploy/model-router | sed -n '1,200p'
  - Promote fallback model: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://control-plane-api/admin/route?action=promote&model=fallback-v1
  - Fetch recent traces: jaeger-query: query by trace id from Datadog/RUM

- Incident naming convention: incident-YYYYMMDD-<sev>-<service> (e.g., incident-20260304-sev1-inference-gateway).

- Contact matrix:
  - PagerDuty: Redwood - Platform SRE (primary)
  - Slack: #incidents (announce only), private incident channel for coordination
  - Pager: escalation to SRE manager, then CTO on prolonged incidents

Revision history

- 2024-09-15: Document created (initial playbook).
- 2025-06-12: Added model-router runbook and model onboarding validation gates.
- 2026-03-04: Expanded game-day schedule, updated SLO thresholds and status-page templates.

For questions or to request an exercise/runbook change, contact the on-call program owner (Asha Patel) or file a request in the eng-sre team backlog (Jira: ENG-IR).
